title: Astronaut Michael Foale Recalls the Scary Space Station Crash of 1997
summary:
Have you ever seen a movie where astronauts have to fix a hole in their spaceship before all the air runs out? That really happened! In 1997, astronaut Michael Foale was on the Russian space station Mir when a cargo ship crashed into it. The crash ripped a hole in the station, and air started hissing out into space. The crew had only 23 minutes of oxygen left to save themselves!

Foale, a British-American astronaut, recently shared his story for a new TV series called "Once Upon a Time in Space." He explained that the crash happened because of a risky test. The Russian space agency wanted to save money. They didn't want to pay Ukraine $2 million for a radar system. So, they asked the crew to dock a cargo ship manually from far away without radar. "The root cause of the accident was trying to save money," Foale says.

The cosmonaut flying the ship, Vasily Tsibliev, couldn't tell how fast it was moving. It hit the station, crumpling a module and bending a solar panel. The crew had to quickly seal the damaged part and stop the station from spinning out of control. They succeeded, but it was terrifying.

Later, Foale was asked to do a spacewalk inside the damaged module to reconnect cables. This was supposed to be done by Vasily, but he was too stressed and failed a medical test. Foale agreed, even though he knew it might embarrass his crewmate. "He took all the blame of the collision on his shoulders, which was unfair," Foale says. The story shows how brave and quick-thinking astronauts have to be in a crisis.
why_it_matters: This story shows that even highly trained astronauts face real danger in space, and that quick thinking and teamwork can save lives—lessons that apply to any crisis at school or home.

background_read: The space station Mir (a Russian home in space that orbited Earth for 15 years, from 1986 to 2001) hosted astronauts from many countries, including the U.S.
In 1997, a risky docking test went wrong, nearly costing the lives of the crew.
Today, former astronaut Michael Foale shares his memories for a TV series called 'Once Upon a Time in Space,' which teaches about the real dangers astronauts face.
Article_Structure: WHO: Astronaut Michael Foale, cosmonaut Vasily Tsibliev, and the Mir crew.
WHAT: A cargo ship collision ripped a hole, causing an air leak with only 23 minutes of oxygen to save themselves.
WHERE: Aboard the Russian space station Mir, orbiting Earth.
WHY: The crash happened because a manual docking test was done without radar to avoid paying $2 million for the system.

perspectives.description: Astronauts like Michael Foale had to act quickly and courageously, showing that bravery and calmness can overcome terrifying situations.
The accident happened because Russia wanted to save $2 million, proving that cutting corners in space can be deadly and cost much more in the long run.
Foale understood that his crewmate Vasily was under huge stress and, to avoid embarrassing him, took on the dangerous spacewalk himself, showing true teamwork.
